sections.h2: Which Dickson County offices set and collect property tax?
sections.html:
Three people in Charlotte matter to a Dickson County owner: the Assessor of Property, Jenny Heath Martin, the Trustee, Glynda Pendergrass, and the county commission. The assessor finds, lists and values every taxable parcel. The trustee sends the bills and takes the money. The twelve commissioners pick the rate when they adopt the budget.

The assessor sits in the Administration Building at 4 Court Square (P.O. Box 270, phone (615) 789-7015). The trustee has a counter in the same courthouse square at 4 Court Square (P.O. Box 220, phone (615) 789-7006) and a branch inside the County Government Building at 303 Henslee Drive in Dickson, reached at (615) 446-8293, option 3. Both counters open at eight and close at four on weekdays.

For mailed payments the trustee's FAQ gives P.O. Box 246, Charlotte, TN 37036, and the Henslee Drive branch has a drop box. The Assessor's election follows the presidential calendar, while other county officials are chosen in the August elections of non-presidential even-numbered years, according to Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What dates matter on a Dickson County tax bill?
sections.html:
The year runs from an assessment on January 1 to a payment window that opens in October and closes at the end of February. Most owners will see only the last two dates on this list, but the earlier ones explain when values can change.

Dates that shape a Dickson County property tax year
WhenEvent
January 1Ownership and condition of each parcel are fixed for the year
By May 20Assessors finish the roll and mail notices of change
June 1The county board of equalization starts hearing complaints
Early OctoberBills mailed; payments accepted from the first Monday
February 28Final day without interest
March 1Balances turn delinquent

Source: Tennessee Comptroller assessment schedule and Dickson County Trustee FAQ.

Bills are addressed to whoever held title on January 1. A person who closes later in the year receives a courtesy copy, but the trustee warns that unpaid tax keeps attaching to the land. The office accepts part-payments toward the current year if the whole bill is cleared by the end of February, and ACH prepayment is offered.

sections.h2: What does a late Dickson County tax balance cost?
sections.html:
A balance still open on March 1 grows by one and a half percent every month, which the trustee describes as 18 percent over a year. The trustee holds it for twelve months and then passes the file to the Chancery Court and a delinquent tax attorney, which adds suit costs and fees on top of the interest.

At the end of that suit the county may sell the parcel at a tax sale. A seller who is behind should ask the title company to pay the arrears out of the sale proceeds before the file reaches court.

Bankruptcy is handled differently. Once a bankruptcy notice arrives, a deputy in the trustee's office files a claim, and federal law bars collection of real or personal property tax until the case is dismissed or discharged. Payment usually follows an installment plan approved by the bankruptcy court.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Dickson County house changes hands?
sections.html:
The buyer inherits responsibility for anything left unpaid at closing, the trustee's FAQ says. How the current year's bill is divided is a matter for the purchase contract and the settlement statement.

Ask the title company for the proration line before you sign. If you never received a bill for a parcel, call the trustee at (615) 789-7006 for a duplicate, because a missing bill does not cancel the debt. A lender that escrows your taxes still needs you to hand over the bill, since the county does not mail one to the mortgage company.

After closing, the deed goes to the Register of Deeds, Shelly Yates, at 4 Court Square (P.O. Box 130, phone (615) 789-5123), who accepts electronic filings through Simplifile, CSC and ePN. Typos in an owner's name or mailing address on the bill are fixed through the assessor.

sections.h2: How do you contest a Dickson County valuation or reduce the bill?
sections.html:
Value disputes begin before the Local Board of Equalization. According to the trustee's FAQ it sits during the first two weeks of June, and you book a slot through the assessor's office. The Comptroller lists the county board's opening day as June 1.

An assessor's informal review can be faster, but the Comptroller says plainly that it is no substitute for an appeal. After a local board decision, the State Board of Equalization takes a petition until August 1 or until 45 days after the local notice was sent, whichever falls later.

  • Homes and farms are assessed at 25 percent of appraised value, and business property at 40 percent
  • The tax equals assessed value over 100, multiplied by the rate
  • On a $306,400 house, the county's Census median, the assessed value would be $76,600

The state also reimburses part of the tax for qualifying seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans. For 2026 the income ceiling is $38,470 counting the 2025 earnings of everyone on the deed, and the benefit covers up to $33,600 of market value. Veterans with a qualifying rating face no income test, and their cap is $175,000. Ask the trustee for the form once the 2026 bill arrives, because the filing window closes five weeks after the delinquency date.

sections.h2: What is Dickson County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
The General Assembly created Dickson County in October 1803, the twenty-fifth of Tennessee's 95 counties, out of land that belonged to Montgomery and Robertson counties. A tornado in 1833 flattened the courthouse square in Charlotte and, by Wikipedia's account, destroyed about 80 percent of the county's records. The replacement courthouse, finished in 1835, is the oldest in continuous use in the state.

The county covers 491 square miles, with the Cumberland River on its northeast side and the Harpeth River on the east. Iron furnaces drove early industry, railroads produced the towns of Dickson, Tennessee City, White Bluff and Burns, and U.S. Highway 70, known as the Broadway of America, crosses it. Montgomery Bell State Park, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the early 1940s, is a short drive east of Dickson. The county school district runs sixteen schools, and Tennessee College of Applied Technology and Nashville State Community College both have campuses in Dickson.

Census QuickFacts add a current picture:

  • 58,662 residents in 2025, 8.0 percent above the 2020 base
  • 80.3 percent of homes occupied by their owners, median rent $1,015
  • Median home value of $306,400 and median household income of $75,003
  • 32.7 minutes mean travel time to work
  • 590 building permits in 2025 and 25,011 housing units

Anyone selling a house with tax owing, an inherited house or one needing work can get the balance and the valuation from the trustee and assessor in two calls.

faqs.q: When can I start paying Dickson County property tax?
faqs.a: From the first Monday of October. Payment without interest is accepted through the last day of February, and March 1 starts the delinquent period.

faqs.q: Where can I pay my Dickson County tax bill in person?
faqs.a: At the trustee's counter in the Charlotte courthouse square or the branch at 303 Henslee Drive in Dickson, from eight to four on weekdays. Mail goes to P.O. Box 246, Charlotte, TN 37036, and local banks take full current-year payments.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax if I buy a Dickson County house mid-year?
faqs.a: You can, because the purchaser is responsible for tax unpaid at closing. Check the settlement statement to see how the year's tax was prorated between you and the seller.

faqs.q: When is the Dickson County board of equalization meeting?
faqs.a: The trustee's FAQ places it in the first two weeks of June, by appointment through the assessor at (615) 789-7015. The Comptroller's calendar lists June 1 as the start date.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for state property tax relief in Dickson County?
faqs.a: Homeowners 65 or older and disabled homeowners with 2025 income at or below $38,470, plus disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses with no income limit. The application goes to the Dickson County Trustee.
